readings.title: A room chosen through a trial
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Residents disagreed about how to use an empty ground-floor room. Some wanted a reading space; others proposed a repair table. Rather than decide from the loudest discussion, the committee organised two temporary sessions for each idea. Volunteers recorded attendance, preparation time and the kind of help people requested. The reading sessions attracted fewer visitors but required little supervision. Repair sessions were busier and needed skilled volunteers. The final plan shared the room between both uses on different days. The trial made the costs and benefits visible enough for residents to discuss a practical arrangement.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: Hearing people who missed the meeting
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A community meeting about weekend activities attracted mostly retired residents. Shift workers and parents of young children were less able to attend. The organiser realised that a room full of people did not necessarily represent the whole neighbourhood. She circulated a short questionnaire through the school and local workplaces and offered a telephone response option. Later replies introduced requests for evening sessions and child-friendly spaces. The committee included a note about how opinions had been collected in its report. It could not claim to have heard everyone, but it had made a deliberate effort to reach beyond the meeting room.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: A decision note that included reasons
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: After choosing new opening hours for a community workshop, the committee posted only the timetable. Members whose suggestions were not adopted felt ignored. The committee then published a short decision note. It listed the main options, explained the limits on staffing and described why the chosen schedule was feasible. The note also named a date for reconsidering the arrangement. Some members still preferred different hours, but they could see that their proposal had been considered. Giving reasons did not remove disagreement. It helped distinguish an unwelcome decision from one made without listening.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: Ending a trial without calling it a failure
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A neighbourhood association tried a weekly tool-swap desk for two months. Attendance was low, and volunteers spent long periods waiting. Interviews revealed that residents liked sharing tools but needed access at unpredictable times. The association ended the weekly desk and created a contact list through which neighbours could arrange exchanges directly. It published what the trial had taught them, including the volunteer time required. Ending the desk was not treated as proof that sharing was a bad idea. The trial had shown that one particular arrangement did not fit the way residents needed the service.

translation.stem:
Translate the following passage into Chinese:
A trial is useful only if people are willing to learn from its results. Continuing an arrangement simply because time has already been spent on it may waste further effort. A better question is whether it meets the needs it was designed to serve. When an approach is changed, explaining what was learned helps others understand the decision. The original goal can remain valuable even when the first method is abandoned.
knowledgePoints: 英译汉：语义准确与中文表达
translation.explanation: 注意only if条件、whether表语从句以及even when让步关系。
translation.referenceAnswer: 只有当人们愿意从结果中学习时，试行才有价值。仅仅因为已经在某项安排上花费了时间就继续它，可能会浪费更多精力。更值得问的是，它是否满足了原本要服务的需求。当方法发生改变时，解释从中学到了什么，有助于其他人理解决定。即使第一种方法被放弃，最初的目标仍然可能具有价值。

writing.stem: Write 100–150 words in English to a neighbourhood committee proposing a trial use for an empty room. Explain the activity, describe what information should be collected, and suggest how a final decision could be made.
knowledgePoints: 写作：任务完成、组织与语言
writing.explanation: 包含试行活动、记录指标以及基于结果公开决策的方法。
writing.sampleAnswer:
Dear Committee Members,
I suggest trying a monthly repair afternoon in the empty ground-floor room. Residents could bring small household items and work with experienced volunteers to explore whether they can be repaired. Clear limits should be agreed on the kinds of tasks volunteers can accept.
A three-session trial would help us understand demand before making a permanent commitment. We should record attendance, preparation time, the help requested and any difficulties with the room. Comments from visitors and volunteers would be useful too.
After the trial, the committee could publish a short summary and invite residents to discuss the results. The final decision should consider both the benefit to users and the effort needed to run the service. If the arrangement needs changing, the trial will still have provided valuable information.
Yours sincerely,
A resident
